fields.mechanism: The use of a two-temperature stage extruder to maintain high polymer viscosity and prevent premature cooling in high-performance polycarbonate
fields.intervention: Equip the 3D printer with a dual-zone heated nozzle and chamber insulation to ensure the second heating zone maintains polycarbonate above its glass transition temperature during layer deposition
fields.expected_effect: Elimination of layer skipping by preventing the loss of material adhesion and flow consistency caused by ambient heat exceeding 35C
fields.falsification_test: Print a 20 mm wall tower with polycarbonate at 35C ambient using both a single-zone and the new two-zone nozzle; measure interlayer shear strength and record video; if the single-zone nozzle shows delamination or skipping while the two-zone nozzle produces continuous layers, the mechanism is verified
fields.mechanism_source_span: maximize the output for a two-temperature stage extruder for PC

fields.intervention: Adjust the print bed temperature to be significantly higher than the 35C ambient threshold (e.g., 80-100C) and calibrate the nozzle velocity to maintain optimal polycarbonate rheology.
fields.expected_effect: Reduces thermal shock between the nozzle and the bed, preventing premature solidification of the layer and eliminating the layer skipping phenomenon.
fields.falsification_test: Print a tower test with polycarbonate at 35C ambient using bed temperatures of 50C, 80C, and 100C; layer skipping should cease at 80C or higher.

fields.mechanism: Two-temperature stage extruder maintains elevated melt/feed temperature to keep polycarbonate above its heat-resistant processing window, preventing premature cooling and loss of inter-layer bonding when ambient conditions approach PC's heat-distortion limit.
fields.intervention: Replace the single-zone hot end with a two-temperature stage extruder for PC, setting the upstream/feed zone to a temperature tuned to keep the melt above the threshold where layer adhesion fails above 35C ambient; monitor and record a single measurement — the inter-layer weld/interface temperature (or equivalently the extrudate surface temperature at deposition) — as the settlement metric.
fields.expected_effect: Layer skipping is eliminated (or sharply reduced) above 35C ambient because the two-stage thermal profile keeps the deposited bead hot enough to fuse with the previously laid layer, compensating for the high ambient temperature that would otherwise flash-cool the extrudate against the heat-resistant PC substrate.
fields.falsification_test: Print the same PC part with the two-temperature stage extruder at a controlled 38C ambient chamber, sweeping the inter-layer deposition temperature setpoint; the layer-skip failure is falsified only if layer skipping disappears once the measured inter-layer deposition temperature stays above the identified threshold across a statistically adequate number of layers, and reappears when that measurement is forced below threshold on an otherwise identical part.
fields.mechanism_source_span: a print test was used to maximize the output for a two-temperature stage extruder for PC.
